recipes.name: Creamy Potato Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of potato soup
1 (2 pound) package frozen hash brown potatoes

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Heat sour cream, condensed soup, and butter in a small pot over low heat.
Combine potatoes, 1 cup cheese, and green onions in a large mixing bowl. Mix in heated soup mixture. Season with salt and pepper. Pour into a 9x13-inch dish. Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 to 45 minutes. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Potato Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This cheesy hash brown casserole combines frozen hash browns, Cheddar cheese, sour cream, and cream of potato soup for an easy, crowd-pleasing side dish.

review.reviewBody: My husband and I loved this! I made it with cream of chicken soup and used less sour cream and butter. I used 50% reduced fat sour cream and butter. I also mixed the cheese throughout and added a little on top. I left it in the oven about ten minutes longer so the cheese could brown on top. Finally, there is no need to thaw hashbrowns as you could break the frozen potatoes down with the hot soup mixture when mixing.

Very good. I reduced the sour cream to one cup and the butter to 2 Tbs based on the other reviews. I also thawed the O'brien potatoes in a colander under running water. I used reduced fat Cream of Celery soup & added garlic powder. I did not heat the soup, butter & cream prior to mixing in; I just mixed everything in a large bowl(stir the soup smooth first) and turned it into a casserole dish to bake. Sprinkled with paprika for color. It turned out very good and I did not have the mess of another saucepan to clean. Good recipe.

Hands down, best creamy potato casserole ever! I did make a few adjustments. I seasoned the potatoes with garlic powder & put all the cheese in the casserole. Then I topped with 1 cup of crushed corn flakes mixed with 1/4 cup melted butter. Also, 5 minutes before it was finished, I also sprinkled on a handful of crushed fried onions.

Loved this! I did use some suggestions and added a few of mine. I defrosted the shredded hash browns and I used 2 cups of soups instead of one. I sprinkled panko crumbs on top of the shredded cheese and baked at 400 for 10 minutes to brown crumbs then 350 for another 30 minutes. It came out fantastic.
I used yellow onion instead of green which I sautéed first w/some ham. I also allowed the hash browns to thaw a bit as per the suggestion of others

Fabulous, but I do have a suggestion. I had to serve this to people I did not know and thought that perhaps not everyone would like the green onions. Some of the people said that it was a little bland too, so... I used the cream of celery soup as people had suggested.
I did not use chopped green onions BUT the last 10 minutes of baking I covered the casserole in Durkee fried onion rings as you would in a greenbean casserole.
I figured that anyone who didn't like onion could just scrape it off. IT WAS WONDERFUL. Oh, I did warm up the potatoes to completely defrost and I did cook it longer that the suggested time. I tried it at the recommended time and it was still a little too firm, so I kept cooking until the potatoes were thoroughly cooked. Different ovens, right???

Delicious! I made a few changes after reading other reviews: parboiled potatoes for 5 minutes; used cream of chicken soup instead of cream of potato; cut back on the sour cream to 1 1/2 cups. For the cheese, I used 1/2 cup shredded swiss cheese and 1/2 cup shredded Monterey Jack. For the topping I substituted a thin layer of Peppridge Farm Stuffing mix, topped with a drizzle of butter. I served this with my holiday meal and received rave reviews even from the pickiest eater. It's a keeper.

Took to a dinner party and it was a hit! I added some goat cheese which just added to the creaminess. I also used the potatoes with onions and peppers so I didn't add more onions. Will definitely make again.

DE-LISH!!! I mixed part mild and part sharp cheese to make this dish (based on another review). We also found that the potatoes need to cook for a good 60 minutes in order for them to soften. Dish was devoured at our event! Everyone loved it. We ended up adding 4 c. cornflakes (crushed) combined with 2/3 stick of butter to make a crunchy topping. Yum!!

suggest cooking the frozen potatoes before adding to the casserole - the potatoes were hard and raw, but the taste of the sauce was good. I will use shredded hash browns rather than the cubed potatoes the next time.

This is a great recipe. I give it four stars because it needs an extra can of soup to be creamy enough. I like to use one can of cream of potato and one can of cream of chicken. I have also used this recipe in the slow cooker on low for eight hours and it turns out great.
I had a 1 lb bag of hash browns (with peppers and onions) in my freezer so I adjusted the recipe to make a smaller batch. This was great!
Made with frozen potato Obrien and it was fantastic! Will cook a bit longer next time but definitely making again and again! Definitely a favorite in our household!

Absolute comfort food heaven! I used cream of broccoli soup, added a handful of crumbled bacon, and used half a pound of ground pork, fried up with some garlic. 
This recipe has so much room for adding your own touch, but is the basis for an amazing family meal :) 
Thank you!!
My granddaughter loved this recipe! New name "cheesy potatoes". The adults did too!

Did not add green onion or potato soup. Added a can of Campbell’s half cream of chicken/cream of mushroom also added a can of cream of celery. Everyone loved it and it was so easy. This is a must have for any good Baptist.

I have always put in fresh mushrooms, sliced and made the soup, can of mushroom. Makes it even better. Didn't use bacon or any meat, it doesn't really need it. And it is a wonderful hit at parties, luncheon, or buffets. I'd suggest this recipe to everyone and anyone. I already have over the years. One of my families favorites.
I too reduced sour cream and butter, neither are that necessary in those amounts. Fresh red onion and garlic improves the taste too. I don't care much for green onions, so this is personal option.
Quick, easy and delicious. I made this for a dinner party with lemon Dijon chicken and everyone loved it.
2 pounds of potatoes will not fit into a 9x13 pan. I just used 1 pound.
I made this exactly as written it was great. I had 10 big eaters for Sunday and all loved it.
